dropped.claim: Despite unique manufacturing flexibility and demonstrated ability to generate operating profits in 2024 and 2022, RYAM faces severe near-term financial distress that creates unacceptable risk at this stage. Stockholders' equity collapsed 56% in one year from $713.9M to $316.6M, operating cash flow fell 88% from $203.6M to $23.9M, and the company holds only $75.4M in cash against $779M in debt with unspecified covenant exposure. While the -$420.7M net loss includes non-cash charges and 2025 results were impacted by temporary disruptions (labor strikes, operational challenges), the severity of the cash flow deterioration and balance sheet erosion—combined with lack of visibility into covenant headroom, ABL availability, and the sustainability of any operational recovery—creates material near-term solvency risk. The potential upside from trade case relief remains uncertain in timing and magnitude. This requires resolution of fundamental liquidity and covenant questions before investment consideration.
